item.title: You'll surely see John Spirit at the UMich/MSU game, so who is he?
item.description: Matt Riley is a University of Michigan guy and John Spirit is as green-and-white as it gets, but Riley always has two things for him when the big football game is scheduled for Ann Arbor: A ticket, and a kind thought. "The guy obviously is wired differently," Riley told me, and yep, that's as clear as the bell on Spirit's ever-present bicycle. But "he hearkens back to a better day of college sports," when things were kinder and less overtly mercenary, and maybe being a fan meant you didn't have to completely grow up. John Spirit first painted himself green from neck to ankles and went to a Michigan State game without a shirt in the early 1990s, and now he's a 52-year-old man getting greened up and doing the same thing. He still rides a green-and-white bike with a Spartan flag fluttering on a long pole extending from the middle of the handlebars. Still engages or amuses some people, and befuddles or annoys others. Still spends most of a football game with his back to the field, exhorting sections of fans to chant "Go green, go white." Still qualifies as East Lansing's most mysterious quasi-public figure, with competing guesses online about what he does and where he does it when he's not attending some manner of sporting event. He'll be at Michigan Stadium on Saturday when the Wolverines face the Spartans at 7:30 p.m. Riley is certain of that, because Spirit called him Monday, Nov. 2, to double-check that a spare ticket was waiting. Television cameras will find him there, because how can they not? Out of 110,000 or so people in attendance, he'll be the only 6-foot-6 bearded adult in what's now a green bodysuit, warmer and less messy than paint or stage makeup, with a big white S on the chest and back. If everyone else is looking at him, the Free Press figured we should, too, even if we're not the eyes he wants. Spirit told Riley he was already camped out for the week in front of Sparty, the 9-foot, 7-inch bronze statue not far from the Red Cedar River on the verdant MSU campus. Each year in the week before the Michigan game, he appoints himself Sparty's guardian and savior from vandals or other forms of evil, a role more formally played by members of the marching band. I could have driven to East Lansing to check on his whereabouts, and maybe I should have, because one of the things to know about Spirit is that he sometimes has a tenuous relationship with accuracy. But he had already answered a call from an intermediary to his battered flip phone and said, "I don't do interviews." That's fine. Vigilance takes concentration. Besides, it's more fun sometimes to ponder a legend than worry about the truth. A long way from reality I did interview Spirit once, the week of the Michigan game in 1997, and almost every verifiable thing he told me turned out to be a fib. item.description: Major League Baseball’s unpopular winter sequel – Lockout II: The Reckoning – has thrown much of its offseason machinations into flux. Not only must teams conduct a significant amount of their business before the industry’s expected shutdown Dec. 1 but do so uncertain what economic system will prevail upon its restart. The notion of a salary cap – even with a year to ease it in – would greatly alter the game’s economic structure. Chasing free agents comes with some uncertainty. But what about trades? Great question. Even a swap that’s decidedly not cash-neutral shouldn’t hamper a team’s flexibility years out. And with most teams committing to landing in a contending-but-not-dominant position – 24 of 30 teams finished with at least 75 wins – filling needs by taking someone else’s ill-fitting part fits that mold. And presuming Carlos Correa come back healthy, the Astros have a little glut on the infield. Paredes is coming off possibly his best all-around season, hitting 25 homers and raising his OBP to a career-high .360. His strikeout rate also fell to a career-low 13.4%. item.title: Bundesliga defender emerges as Barcelona’s leading target as €65m release clause offers an opportunity
item.description: Bundesliga defender emerges as Barcelona’s leading target as €65m release clause offers an opportunity According to SPORT , RB Leipzig defender Castello Lukeba has emerged as Barcelona’s priority target to reinforce the centre-back position. Moreover, the French defender has taken an important step towards a potential transfer to Catalonia after changing his representatives and joining the agency that also manages Barça star Jules Kounde, ‘Excellence Sport’. Lukeba at the top of Barcelona’s wishlist Barcelona have been monitoring Lukeba for quite some time now. His performances with RB Leipzig have seen him get established as one of the most talented young centre-backs in Europe. The fact that he is a left-footed central defender and possesses the qualities that would make him a very good fit into Hansi Flick’s tactical setup have made him an attractive option for the La Liga champions. After all, the 23-year-old defender combines physical strength, aerial ability and composure in possession. That, coupled with his ground speed, could make him suitable addition in Barcelona’s high-defensive line system under Flick. Castello Lukeba on Barcelona’s agenda. (Photo by Stuart Franklin/Getty Images) The Catalan club had previously explored the possibility of signing him but decided against making a major investment in central defence. However, he is back on the agenda and is seen as a more appealing target compared to Inter Milan’s Alessandro Bastoni. Lukeba open to Barcelona move Furthermore, the report states that Lukeba keen to leave Germany in search of a project capable of competing for major trophies. Barcelona are understood to be his preferred destination , and his change of representation could help facilitate discussions over a possible move. After all, the Blaugrana’s sporting director Deco recently held a meeting with a representative from Excellence Sport, with a move for the Frenchman among the topics discussed. Lukeba’s release clause set to drop to €65m in the summer. (Photo by George Wood/Getty Images) However, as things stand, a January transfer is considered highly unlikely, with RB Leipzig unwilling to let the defender leave during the winter window. Things could be much easier in the summer, though, as Lukeba’s release clause is set to decrease from €80 million to €65 million in June, providing Barcelona an opportunity. That figure could potentially be negotiated further if the player makes his preference for a move to Catalonia clear. His salary is also expected to be more manageable than that of Bastoni. Barcelona have already begun making enquiries, but any serious attempt to complete the transfer is expected to take place in the summer.

item.title: Texas A&M at South Carolina: Three areas to watch in Week 10 road trip
item.description: Texas A&M football faces a difficult task in Week 10, as the Aggies travel to take on one of college football's hottest teams. This isn't the same South Carolina team Texas A&M played in College Station last year. The No. 21 Gamecocks boast a 5-3 overall record, including a 3-3 mark in SEC play, and are coming off three-straight conference wins over then-ranked No. 16 Florida, No. 11 Tennessee and Oklahoma. South Carolina's back-to-back wins over the Gators and Volunteers marked the third time under head coach Shane Beamer the team has posted consecutive top-25 wins. That success has largely come from incredible performances by senior quarterback LaNorris Sellers, who posted his fifth career 300-plus-yard passing game against the Sooners in Week 9. Texas A&M must stop Sellers and South Carolina's high-powered offense, which enters Saturday's contest ranked the No. 2 unit in the league. However, the Aggies' defense flashed at times in the 31-20 loss to No. 13 Alabama, notching two interceptions and tying the season-high with two sacks. A road win in one of the nation's most hostile environments would go a long way toward building momentum, but it is a tall ask for a team that has failed to find its footing offensively. Here are three areas to watch in Texas A&M's road trip to Columbia: Texas A&M's defensive line vs. Sellers Sellers was on a tear in October, throwing for over 200 yards every game, including a season-high 301 in South Carolina's 42-25 victory at Oklahoma. He also has back-to-back outings with 90-plus rushing yards, flashing his outstanding athleticism. To stop the 6-foot-3, 238-pound gunslinger, Texas A&M's defensive line must be able to apply pressure and force him to make errant throws. Sellers' decision-making hasn't been the greatest at times, tied for second in the SEC with seven interceptions, which could provide the Aggies' secondary an opportunity to force turnovers. If defensive coordinator Lyle Hemphill can draw up some ways to keep Sellers off-balance by collapsing the pocket, Texas A&M's defense could find success. Physical tackling and the pass rush will be integral in slowing down South Carolina's electric quarterback. Texas A&M's offensive line vs. Dylan Stewart On the opposite side of the gridiron, South Carolina boasts one of the most-feared edge rushers in college football. Since Beamer benched him after the Gamecocks' Week 9 loss to Alabama, Stewart has compiled seven solo tackles, including 2.5 tackles for loss, and two sacks. The 6-foot-5, 250-pounder's elite speed and physicality are why he leads the 2027 NFL Draft class in pass rush efficiency. item.title: USA women's hockey goes for back-to-back gold medals at Women's World Championship
item.description: The U.S. women’s national hockey team looks to win back-to-back gold medals at the 2026 Women’s World Championship in Denmark this week as the countdown to the 2030 Winter Olympics in France begins. American women's hockey captain Hilary Knight may have played in her last Olympic Games earlier this year, but her international career is far from over. Knight is set to appear in her 16th Women's World Championship, where she's won a record 10 gold medals while setting all-time records for goals (67), assists (53) and points (120). The U.S. and Canada have faced off against each other in every Women's World Championships gold-medal game since the first tournament was held in 1990. That's 24 consecutive world championship finals. The longtime rivals could extend that streak to 25 in Denmark at the 2026 IIHF Women’s World Championship, which will begin on Friday, Nov. 6, and run through Monday, Nov. 16. Highlights: Canada women's hockey defeats USA in Olympic rematch Fans got a preview of the potential final matchup when USA and Canada squared off in two exhibition matches ahead of the tournament last month. Canada's new-look roster won the first game 5-3 in Ontario on Oct. 28 to snap the Americans' eight-game win streak dating back to April 2025, which included overtime gold-medal wins over Canada at the 2025 Women's World Championship in Czechia and 2026 Winter Olympics in Milan, Italy. Canada did so without Marie-Philip Poulin, who'll miss the tournament while recovering from ACL and meniscus surgery, marking the first time Poulin won't be on the Canadian roster at a major tournament since 2008. However, the Americans bounced back with a dominant 4-0 win over the Canadians in the second tune-up game in Michigan on Oct. 30. Kirsten Simms, Tessa Janecke, Hannah Bilka and Joy Dunne all scored in the rout, while Caroline Harvey and Laila Edwards each added two assists each. "We were just shaking the rust off," said Knight, who finished with one goal across two pre-tournament games. "We had a slow start and just trying to feel the game out a little bit. And so I think that's what makes this win better because it really did feel like a team win. Everyone was kind of going on all cylinders and that's what you want, especially going into a major international tournament when it's best on best." USA, the defending champions, will look to win back-to-back World titles for the first time since 2019. In addition to USA and Canada, the field also includes host country Denmark, Germany, Austria, Finland, Japan, Czechia, Sweden and Switzerland, which won the Olympic bronze medal at the 2026 Winter Olympics. Here's what you need to know about the tournament, as the new Olympic cycle begins: How to watch U.S. women's hockey in World Championship? The U.S. women's hockey team is set to compete in the 2026 IIHF Women’s World Championship in Herning and Esbjerg, Denmark from Nov. 6-16. All USA matchups will be broadcast on NHL Network and available to stream on Fubo.

item.title: John Harbaugh's Giants take aim at ending 13-game nightmare in Philly
item.description: EAST RUTHERFORD - This is inherited franchise history for John Harbaugh and the 2026 New York Giants , not earned. But it's notable history nonetheless, resurfacing every time the Giants' buses hit the Turnpike and travel to what has become a house of horrors for this organization. The head coaches have changed. The players have changed. So have the circumstances. The Giants have found nothing but frustration, agony and despair in Philadelphia over the past decade-plus, however. There's a total of 13 consecutive losses, including the trouncing at the hands of the Eagles in the 2022 NFC Divisional Round of the playoffs that ended Brian Daboll's first season as head coach. The Giants have not won at Lincoln Financial Field since 2013, and on that day when they last did, Josh Brown kicked five field goals, Peyton Hillis was the leading rusher, and Victor Cruz was the leading receiver for Tom Coughlin's team. Chip Kelly's offense with the Eagles was all the NFL could talk about back then. Michael Vick was at quarterback in place of an injured Nick Foles. And Eli Manning passed Phil Simms as the franchise's all-time leader in yards passing in that game. Here's a look at what Big Blue has endured against the Eagles on the road in what has become a bitter, one-sided rivalry, especially at the Linc, where the reception for the visitors is really unlike any other. "Plenty of boos and middle fingers for us," former Giants wide receiver Darius Slayton said. Let's go back in time and revisit the Giants' last 13 trips to the Linc, where the City of Brotherly Love would be more appropriately named for Big Blue if it were the Place Where Hopes and Dreams Get Shattered. The Harbaugh Giants (4-2-1) have a chance to build on their lead in the NFC East against the 2-6 Eagles, who have lost six straight games and are making another change at quarterback. They'll start Joe Milton as Tanner McKee, who filled in for the injured Jalen Hurts, is benched. These are the ghosts of Giants past, unavoidable and agonizing memories brought about by the mere chanting of "Fly Eagles Fly," haunted by the all too familiar sounds of a fight song and more than a decade of pain: 2014: Eagles 27, Giants 0 If there was one image to symbolize the Giants' fate in Philly, it is this one: Victor Cruz, crying and holding his hands to his face in disbelief after he tore the patellar tendon in his right knee while leaping for a pass on fourth down from the Eagles' 3 in the third quarter. The Eagles sacked Eli Manning six times, snapping the Giants' three-game winning streak in which they had scored more than 30 points in each victory. item.title: Robinson returns to Sussex as director of cricket
item.description: Mark Robinson enjoyed success as head coach of Surrey and more recently Warwickshire [Getty Images] Mark Robinson has returned to Sussex as director of cricket. Robinson, 59, spent five years as a player at the club and a decade as head coach. He led Sussex to County Championship Division One titles in 2006 and 2007, as well as the Twenty20 Cup in 2009, the Friends Provident Trophy in 2006 and the Pro40 National League in 2008 and 2009. Paul Farbrace had been set to switch roles from Sussex head coach to director of cricket, but he joined Lancashire last month amid financial troubles at Hove. Robinson's new position is a part-time role and he will continue as director of cricket at Brighton Aldridge Community Academy. "I'm delighted to be back at Hove in a position where I can play my part in helping Sussex continue to be one of the most respected clubs in the country," Robinson told the club website. Sussex needed an emergency bailout from the England and Wales Cricket Board after a £1.3m trading loss in 2025, and were docked 12 Championship points for sustained operating losses, plus a point in each white-ball competition. "We have taken some hits in the last year and as a club have some work still to be done, and I am determined to contribute to ensure a bright future here at Sussex," Robinson added. "I first joined this club in 1997, just after the revolution following the loss of most of its senior players and captain. I was just one small building block that helped build an era of unqualified success. "Work has already started to ensure that we do that again. Sussex is a special club and I'm delighted to be back." Robinson guided England Women to 2017 World Cup glory and also enjoyed success as Warwickshire head coach, securing another County Championship Division One title, in 2021. "I cannot imagine a better person to become our director of cricket," said Sussex's acting chief executive Alex Paterson.

item.description: Kentucky women’s basketball is absolutely loaded with talent from top to bottom this season. The Cats put it on full display Tuesday, rolling to an 85-42 win over Morehead State. Emily McDonald and Savvy Swords arrived in Lexington with massive expectations, and they both made an immediate impact in their college debuts. McDonald wasted no time finding her offensive rhythm, finishing with 10 points and two rebounds. Watching them operate together on the court felt like a seamless continuation of their high school days at Long Island Lutheran High School in Brookville, New York. item.title: Maresca backs goalkeeper Donnarumma after Leipzig error
item.description: Maresca backs goalkeeper Donnarumma after Leipzig error Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca admitted Gianluigi Donnarumma made a mistake in their 3-2 Champions League victory over RB Leipzig but defended the goalkeeper following his error. City secured all three points in Germany despite twice conceding, with Donnarumma coming under scrutiny for his role in Leipzig’s first equaliser. Asked whether he was concerned by the Italian’s mistake, Maresca said: “It’s not a concern, but it’s a mistake. We recognise, he knows, that it’s a mistake. “Now it’s 48 hours, Nottingham Forest away, we need to be focused on that. Then we have the international break and we can see different things.” Maresca was later asked whether the upcoming international break would provide an opportunity to reassess his goalkeeping situation, but the City boss insisted he was not considering making changes. “At the moment I’m not thinking about the international break and the goalkeeper situation,” he explained. “Because we are talking about the mistake, but a few minutes before the mistake, he has done a save that any keeper in the world is not going to do that save. “So it’s always a balance. And Gigi knows that the first goal was not good. But again, he’s going to do better.” City’s defensive performances have come under increasing scrutiny following a run of seven matches without a clean sheet, with Maresca admitting his side must cut out individual errors. “I think both goals are quite silly goals that we can avoid,” he said. “I think we are creating, since day one, many chances in each game, but we need to avoid two conceded silly goals.” Maresca also rejected suggestions that City’s defensive struggles were a consequence of his tactical approach, instead pointing to individual mistakes. “Probably in the last five or six goals we conceded in all the competitions, they are almost individual mistakes. So it’s not about the system,” he said. “It’s not about the defensive line or midfielder or the offensive line. In this moment it’s more individual mistakes that for sure we need to do better and to avoid that.” Stay up to date with all the latest Manchester City news by joining our Man City WhatsApp channel .

item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo ends Portugal career
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Portugal's Cristiano Ronaldo reacts after the 2026 FIFA World Cup group K soccer match between Portugal and DR Congo at Houston Stadium. (is associated with: «Cristiano Ronaldo ends Portugal career») Tom Weller/dpa Cristiano Ronaldo has ended his Portugal career with immediate effect, the 41-year-old football star said on social media on Thursday. The forward walked out on the national team during the last international break after a row with coach Jorge Jesus over playing time. He was given a 30-day ban by the Portuguese Football Federation but had been expected to return to the fold for Nations League matches in November. But he has now decided to call time on an international career which has heralded a men's record 146 goals. "To the Portuguese people, the day has come for me to hand back the number seven shirt of our national team," he said in a video. Ronaldo will still continue to play for Saudi club side Al Nassr as he chases 1,000 career goals. He had previously indicated he could retire completely next year.
